+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Reproduce authentication timeout handling after a short pg_authid lock wait.
+
+This test is authored but unexecuted. It opens a real MD5-authenticated TCP
+connection while another session holds ACCESS EXCLUSIVE on pg_authid, observes
+the target's pending AccessShareLock through the lock-holder session, then
+releases the barrier. The test intentionally does not use lock_timeout, which
+was added after this source revision.
+"""
+import json
+import os
+from pathlib import Path
+import select
+import shutil
+import socket
+import subprocess
+import sys
+import tempfile
+import time
+
+
+IID = "postgres__postgres-commit-592b615d71ca"
+BIN = Path("/opt/pg/bin")
+SERVICE_USER = "bench"
+TARGET_USER = "probe"
+TARGET_PASSWORD = "acrepair-592b-password"
+RESULT_PREFIX = "CHECK_RESULT="
+READ_BUFFERS = {}
+
+
+def command(args, *, env=None, timeout=90):
+    return subprocess.run(args, stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL, stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
+                          stderr=subprocess.STDOUT, text=True, env=env,
+                          timeout=timeout)
+
+
+def free_port():
+    with socket.socket() as sock:
+        sock.bind(("127.0.0.1", 0))
+        return sock.getsockname()[1]
+
+
+def read_line(proc, timeout):
+    fd = proc.stdout.fileno()
+    buffer = READ_BUFFERS.get(fd, b"")
+    deadline = time.monotonic() + timeout
+    while True:
+        newline = buffer.find(b"\n")
+        if newline >= 0:
+            line, buffer = buffer[:newline], buffer[newline + 1:]
+            READ_BUFFERS[fd] = buffer
+            return line.rstrip(b"\r").decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
+        remaining = deadline - time.monotonic()
+        if remaining <= 0:
+            READ_BUFFERS[fd] = buffer
+            return None
+        ready, _, _ = select.select([fd], [], [], remaining)
+        if not ready:
+            READ_BUFFERS[fd] = buffer
+            return None
+        chunk = os.read(fd, 4096)
+        if not chunk:
+            READ_BUFFERS[fd] = buffer
+            return None
+        buffer += chunk
+
+
+def read_marker(proc, marker, timeout=15):
+    deadline = time.monotonic() + timeout
+    observed = []
+    while time.monotonic() < deadline:
+        line = read_line(proc, max(0.01, deadline - time.monotonic()))
+        if line is None:
+            break
+        observed.append(line)
+        if line == marker:
+            return observed
+    raise TimeoutError("psql did not emit marker " + marker + ": " + "\\n".join(observed[-20:]))
+
+
+def emit_error(reason, details=None):
+    print(RESULT_PREFIX + json.dumps({"instance_id": IID, "harness_error": reason,
+                                      "details": details or {}}, ensure_ascii=False),
+          flush=True)
+    # The evaluator parses CHECK_RESULT only after a zero runner exit code.
+    return 0
+
+
+def main():
+    if os.geteuid() == 0:
+        return emit_error("TEST_MUST_RUN_AS_UNPRIVILEGED_POSTGRES_SERVICE_USER")
+    if any(not (BIN / binary).is_file() for binary in ("initdb", "pg_ctl", "psql")):
+        return emit_error("PINNED_POSTGRES_BINARIES_MISSING")
+
+    case_dir = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="acrepair-592b-auth-timeout-"))
+    data_dir = case_dir / "data"
+    socket_dir = case_dir / "socket"
+    socket_dir.mkdir(mode=0o700)
+    log_file = case_dir / "postgres.log"
+    port = free_port()
+    started = False
+    locker = None
+    target = None
+    try:
+        initialized = command([str(BIN / "initdb"), "-D", str(data_dir), "-A", "trust"],
+                              timeout=300)
+        if initialized.returncode:
+            return emit_error("INITDB_FAILED", {"output": initialized.stdout[-4000:]})
+
+        # Local administration remains trust-authenticated. The target path
+        # uses MD5 so ClientAuthentication must look up the role in pg_authid.
+        (data_dir / "pg_hba.conf").write_text(
+            "local all all trust\n"
+            "host all all 127.0.0.1/32 md5\n"
+            "host all all ::1/128 reject\n",
+            encoding="utf-8")
+
+        startup = command([str(BIN / "pg_ctl"), "-D", str(data_dir), "-l", str(log_file),
+                           "-o", f"-k {socket_dir} -p {port} -c listen_addresses=127.0.0.1 "
+                                  "-c authentication_timeout=60",
+                           "-w", "start"], timeout=120)
+        if startup.returncode:
+            return emit_error("POSTGRES_START_FAILED", {"output": startup.stdout[-4000:]})
+        started = True
+
+        admin = command([str(BIN / "psql"), "-X", "-A", "-t", "-q", "-v",
+                         "ON_ERROR_STOP=1", "-h", str(socket_dir), "-p", str(port),
+                         "-U", SERVICE_USER, "-d", "postgres", "-c",
+                         f"CREATE ROLE {TARGET_USER} LOGIN PASSWORD '{TARGET_PASSWORD}';"],
+                        timeout=30)
+        if admin.returncode:
+            return emit_error("TARGET_ROLE_SETUP_FAILED", {"output": admin.stdout[-4000:]})
+
+        target_env = os.environ.copy()
+        target_env["PGPASSWORD"] = TARGET_PASSWORD
+        target_args = [str(BIN / "psql"), "-X", "-A", "-t", "-q", "-v",
+                       "ON_ERROR_STOP=1", "-h", "127.0.0.1", "-p", str(port),
+                       "-U", TARGET_USER, "-d", "postgres", "-c", "SELECT 1;"]
+
+        # This control confirms host MD5 authentication is active and the
+        # valid credential works when no pg_authid lock is held.
+        unblocked = command(target_args, env=target_env, timeout=30)
+        unblocked_ok = (unblocked.returncode == 0 and unblocked.stdout.strip() == "1")
+        if not unblocked_ok:
+            return emit_error("UNBLOCKED_MD5_LOGIN_CONTROL_FAILED",
+                              {"returncode": unblocked.returncode,
+                               "output": unblocked.stdout[-4000:]})
+
+        locker = subprocess.Popen(
+            [str(BIN / "psql"), "-X", "-A", "-t", "-q", "-v", "ON_ERROR_STOP=1",
+             "-h", str(socket_dir), "-p", str(port), "-U", SERVICE_USER,
+             "-d", "postgres"],
+            stdin=subprocess.PIPE, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,
+            text=True, bufsize=1)
+        locker.stdin.write("BEGIN;\nLOCK TABLE pg_authid IN ACCESS EXCLUSIVE MODE;\n"
+                           "SELECT 'LOCK_HELD';\n")
+        locker.stdin.flush()
+        read_marker(locker, "LOCK_HELD")
+
+        # Start the TCP login only after the exclusive lock is confirmed.
+        target_started_at = time.monotonic()
+        target = subprocess.Popen(target_args, stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL,
+                                  stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,
+                                  text=True, env=target_env)
+
+        waiter_seen = False
+        deadline = time.monotonic() + 15
+        poll_sql = (
+            "SELECT CASE WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_locks "
+            "WHERE relation = 'pg_authid'::regclass "
+            "AND mode = 'AccessShareLock' AND NOT granted) "
+            "THEN 'LOCK_WAITING' ELSE 'NO_WAITER' END;"
+        )
+        while time.monotonic() < deadline:
+            locker.stdin.write(poll_sql + "\n")
+            locker.stdin.flush()
+            response = read_line(locker, 2)
+            if response == "LOCK_WAITING":
+                waiter_seen = True
+                break
+            if target.poll() is not None:
+                break
+            if response is None:
+                break
+            time.sleep(0.02)
+
+        waited_seconds = round(time.monotonic() - target_started_at, 3)
+        locker.stdin.write("ROLLBACK;\nSELECT 'LOCK_RELEASED';\n")
+        locker.stdin.flush()
+        read_marker(locker, "LOCK_RELEASED", timeout=10)
+
+        try:
+            target_output, _ = target.communicate(timeout=30)
+        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
+            target.kill()
+            target_output, _ = target.communicate(timeout=5)
+            return emit_error("TARGET_LOGIN_DID_NOT_FINISH_AFTER_LOCK_RELEASE",
+                              {"output": target_output[-4000:]})
+
+        target_ok = (waiter_seen and target.returncode == 0 and
+                     target_output.strip() == "1")
+        timeout_signature = (target.returncode != 0 and
+                             "statement timeout" in target_output.lower())
+        checks = [
+            {"name": "unblocked_password_login_succeeds", "kind": "control",
+             "passed": unblocked_ok,
+             "actual": {"returncode": unblocked.returncode,
+                        "output": unblocked.stdout.strip()},
+             "expected": "a valid MD5-authenticated login succeeds without a catalog lock"},
+            {"name": "connection_waited_for_pg_authid_access_share_lock", "kind": "control",
+             "passed": waiter_seen,
+             "actual": {"waiter_observed": waiter_seen, "waited_seconds": waited_seconds},
+             "expected": "pg_locks shows the new authentication backend waiting for AccessShareLock on pg_authid"},
+            {"name": "authentication_survives_short_pg_authid_lock_wait", "kind": "target",
+             "passed": target_ok,
+             "actual": {"returncode": target.returncode, "output": target_output[-4000:],
+                        "waited_seconds": waited_seconds},
+             "expected": "after the lock is released well before authentication_timeout, the valid-password connection completes SELECT 1"},
+        ]
+        print(RESULT_PREFIX + json.dumps({
+            "instance_id": IID,
+            "checks": checks,
+            "reproduced": waiter_seen and unblocked_ok and timeout_signature,
+            "origin": "generated_from_problem_statement_and_fix_diff",
+            "scope_note": "A two-session lock barrier models VACUUM FULL's conflicting AccessExclusiveLock on pg_authid; the target uses MD5 authentication, and no lock_timeout GUC is assumed.",
+        }, ensure_ascii=False), flush=True)
+        return 0
+    finally:
+        if target is not None and target.poll() is None:
+            try:
+                target.kill()
+                target.communicate(timeout=5)
+            except Exception:
+                pass
+        if locker is not None and locker.poll() is None:
+            try:
+                locker.stdin.write("ROLLBACK;\n\\q\n")
+                locker.stdin.flush()
+                locker.communicate(timeout=5)
+            except Exception:
+                try:
+                    locker.kill()
+                    locker.communicate(timeout=5)
+                except Exception:
+                    pass
+        if started:
+            try:
+                command([str(BIN / "pg_ctl"), "-D", str(data_dir), "-m", "immediate",
+                         "-w", "stop"], timeout=30)
+            except Exception:
+                pass
+        shutil.rmtree(case_dir, ignore_errors=True)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    try:
+        sys.exit(main())
+    except Exception as exc:
+        print(RESULT_PREFIX + json.dumps({"instance_id": IID,
+                                          "harness_error": type(exc).__name__ + ": " + str(exc)},
+                                         ensure_ascii=False), flush=True)
+        sys.exit(0)

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Case-specific evaluation entry for postgres__postgres-commit-592b615d71ca; injected after agent repair."""
+import hashlib
+import json
+from pathlib import Path
+import runpy
+import sys
+
+INSTANCE_ID = 'postgres__postgres-commit-592b615d71ca'
+REQUIRED_CHECK_IDS = ['unblocked_password_login_succeeds', 'connection_waited_for_pg_authid_access_share_lock', 'authentication_survives_short_pg_authid_lock_wait']
+TEST_STATUS = 'authored_unexecuted'
+EXPECTED_FILES = {'case_body.py': '3254a7f8b2dd542892c01170ecb1b97829465cc876d5d3b2afd60db5a8c573e0', 'record.json': '7e149ee79cba3339e7e5fdeceebdf8f43ae314b5406a5d10d694338cba441d5b', 'scenario.json': '97008128f6828d40ba5b1fe7cff62931bc2ca4aba68c3f2b7d719d659d4d4f13', 'scenario.sql': '322b6f351e3411f20720320c7ea99718410b7a761b7f3858739e2ae5d5d5e80f'}
+
+
+def error(reason, **details):
+    print('CHECK_RESULT=' + json.dumps({
+        'instance_id': INSTANCE_ID, 'status': 'BLOCKED' if TEST_STATUS == 'dependency_placeholder' else 'ERROR',
+        'harness_error': reason, 'required_check_ids': REQUIRED_CHECK_IDS,
+        'checks': [], 'reproduced': False, **details,
+    }, ensure_ascii=False), flush=True)
+    return 2
+
+
+def main():
+    folder = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
+    for name, digest in EXPECTED_FILES.items():
+        path = folder / name
+        if not path.is_file() or hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest() != digest:
+            return error('CASE_TEST_ASSET_MISMATCH', asset=name)
+    scenario = json.loads((folder / 'scenario.json').read_text(encoding='utf-8'))
+    if scenario.get('instance_id') != INSTANCE_ID:
+        return error('SCENARIO_INSTANCE_MISMATCH')
+    if TEST_STATUS == 'dependency_placeholder':
+        return error('DEPENDENCY_BLOCKED', blockers=scenario.get('blockers', []),
+                     dependencies=scenario.get('dependency_requirements', []))
+    sys.path.insert(0, str(folder))
+    runpy.run_path(str(folder / 'case_body.py'), run_name='__main__')
+    return 0
+
+
+if __name__ == '__main__':
+    raise SystemExit(main())
problem_statement:
Fix incorrect timeout handling during initial authentication transaction.

The statement start timestamp was not set before initiating the transaction
that is used to look up client authentication information in pg_authid.
In consequence, enable_sig_alarm computed a wrong value (far in the past)
for statement_fin_time.  That didn't have any immediate effect, because the
timeout alarm was set without reference to statement_fin_time; but if we
subsequently blocked on a lock for a short time, CheckStatementTimeout
would consult the bogus value when we cancelled the lock timeout wait,
and then conclude we'd timed out, leading to immediate failure of the
connection attempt.  Thus an innocent "vacuum full pg_authid" would cause
failures of concurrent connection attempts.  Noted while testing other,
more serious consequences of vacuum full on system catalogs.

We should set the statement timestamp before StartTransactionCommand(),
so that the transaction start timestamp is also valid.  I'm not sure if
there are any non-cosmetic effects of it not being valid, but the xact
timestamp is at least sent to the statistics machinery.

Back-patch to 9.0.  Before that, the client authentication timeout was done
outside any transaction and did not depend on this state to be valid.
